title: Lake Nasser cruises: Abu Simbel by water
standfirst: Abu Simbel lies far south of Aswan, on the shore of Lake Nasser, and isn’t on a Luxor–Aswan cruise. A few ships cruise the lake instead, between Aswan and Abu Simbel. It is one of the [[up]].

sections.heading: Where the lake cruises sail
paragraphs: Lake Nasser cruises sail between Aswan and Abu Simbel, south of the Nile’s Luxor–Aswan stretch. Some ships moor beside the temples, so you see them from the water as well as on foot. Each ship’s page shows its own nights, direction and sailing dates.

sections.heading: The temples of Abu Simbel
paragraphs: Two rock-cut temples of Ramesses II: the Great Temple, with its four colossal seated statues of the king, and the smaller temple of his queen, Nefertari. In the 1960s both were cut into blocks and moved higher up, away from the rising waters of the new lake.

sections.heading: By water or by road
paragraphs: Most visitors come on a day trip from Aswan: about three to four hours each way by road, usually leaving before dawn, or a short flight. A Lake Nasser cruise reaches the temples by water instead.
Twice a year, around 22 February and 22 October, the rising sun reaches the inner sanctuary of the Great Temple. Those days are very busy.

faqs.q: Does a Luxor to Aswan cruise go to Abu Simbel?
faqs.a: No. Abu Simbel lies far south of Aswan. Luxor–Aswan cruises offer it as an optional excursion from Aswan; a Lake Nasser cruise sails there.

faqs.q: How many nights is a Lake Nasser cruise?
faqs.a: It depends on the ship. Each ship’s page shows its own nights and sailing dates.

faqs.q: Do Lake Nasser cruises stop at the temples?
faqs.a: Some ships moor beside the temples of Abu Simbel. Check each ship’s programme.
